recommendation: Keep the no-change audit for current FHIR core. Any remaining historical R4B technical-correction work belongs in the publication/rendering-tooling path, not in a current Resource StructureDefinition source edit.
issue_request: FHIR-37544 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I issue raised against R4B because the HTML presentation for Resource.id rendered the type as string even though the underlying definition had id constraints.
initial_application: No core source commit mentioning FHIR-37544 was found. The current active Resource source already uses FHIRPath System.String with structuredefinition-fhir-type valueUrl id, and related FHIR-25274 work documented that constrained-simple-string pattern.
additional_context: The R4B published HTML still reproduces the historic defect by linking Resource.id to string, while R4B conformance JSON and current source carry fhir-type id. The current CI build renders Resource.id as id. Zulip and Confluence evidence confirm the issue was understood and approved as a rendering/tooling correction, with HL7/kindling#78 filed for the renderer.
reconciliation: Made no source change. The current core checkout is correct and editing Resource.id would either duplicate existing documentation or obscure why the ElementDefinition code remains FHIRPath System.String while the fhir-type extension supplies id constraints.

related_jiras.note: Explains and documents the System.String plus structuredefinition-fhir-type pattern that makes Resource.id carry id constraints without primitive child elements.
Nearby tooling decision about fhir-type values on Element/BackboneElement ids, but not the Resource.id R4B rendering defect decided here.
Nearby primitive snapshot-generation discussion mentioned in the Zulip thread, but it concerns other primitive datatypes and is not needed to decide FHIR-37544.
